title: Reimburse Ikigai Info Governance Action Deposit.

rationale.summary: Vote: NO. For this TreasuryWithdrawals (active), downside risk and/or weak safeguards outweighed demonstrated benefit in the current evidence set. Decisive reason: a material claim is unsupported — "A Cardano node bug permitted an unregistered stake key to be used in the governance action, preventing the submitter from recovering the 100,000 ADA deposit." — so cost or precedent may outweigh the benefit. Weighed against it: the proposal substantiates "An Info governance action titled Cardanoの生きがい - Ikigai - was submitted in September 2024 soon after the Chang hard fork." and clears the evidence gates. What would change this vote to YES: Provide independent evidence for: The proposer says there was significant community sentiment that the Ikigai deposit should be reimbursed; Provide milestone-gated disbursement. Residual uncertainty: Treasury flow signal is in unsustainable regime, ratio 2.14 (total inflow (tau + donations) vs enacted withdrawals); advisory penalty applied. Confidence context: score -0.25; confidence 75.2%.
rationale.summary_raw: Advisory model lean was -0.030 (display cap ±0.05) and had zero influence on the binding score: The request has a clear narrow purpose and small delivery surface, but the deterministic assessment marks the evidence as thin, and the highest-materiality claims about the node bug, non-recovery, prior treasury funding, and NCL adherence are mostly asserted rather than evidenced in the document.
top_fixes: Provide independent evidence for: The proposer says there was significant community sentiment that the Ikigai deposit should be reimbursed.

sections.title: Intake
sections.conclusion: Baseline fields and source anchors establish whether the proposal can be reviewed at all.

sections.title: Claims and evidence
findings: Proposal document read by reasoning layer: yes
Requested: Reimburse the Ikigai Info governance action submitter for a lost 100,000 ADA deposit plus 3,000 ADA for missed staking rewards.
Recipient: Ikigai Info governance action submitter; exact name and recipient address not stated in document
Deliverables: Instant on-chain treasury withdrawal to the intended recipient upon enactment
Deadline/expiry: Instantly as part of governance action enactment on-chain
Claim (governance, supported_in_proposal, medium materiality): An Info governance action titled Cardanoの生きがい - Ikigai - was submitted in September 2024 soon after the Chang hard fork.

Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, low materiality): The Ikigai action was symbolic and asked the community to agree with a statement thanking contributors and expressing hope for Cardano's future.

Claim (technical, proposer_asserted, high materiality): A Cardano node bug permitted an unregistered stake key to be used in the governance action, preventing the submitter from recovering the 100,000 ADA deposit.
Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, medium materiality): The proposal points to an external governance record for the prior Ikigai action.
Claim (adoption, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): The proposer says there was significant community sentiment that the Ikigai deposit should be reimbursed.

Claim (economic, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The requested withdrawal is 103,000 ADA, consisting of the original 100,000 ADA deposit plus 3,000 ADA for lost staking rewards at 2% per annum.
missing: Independent evidence for: A Cardano node bug permitted an unregistered stake key to be used in the governance action, preventing the submitter from recovering the 100,000 ADA deposit.
Independent evidence for: The proposer says there was significant community sentiment that the Ikigai deposit should be reimbursed.

Independent evidence for: The proposer states there are no costs, expenses, audit budget, refund circumstances, or administrator custody associated with this withdrawal because funds would be distributed directly on-chain.
Independent evidence for: The proposer states the recipient has not previously received treasury funds and that the requested amount does not exceed the current Net Change Limit.
sections.conclusion: Each claim must map to replayable public evidence; proposer assertions alone are not enough for confidence.

sections.title: Treasury analysis
findings: Six-month treasury flow regime: unsustainable (basis: total inflow (tau + donations) vs enacted withdrawals)
missing: milestone-gated disbursement
sustainability path
cost-benefit clarity
sections.conclusion: Treasury votes require a higher bar because they consume shared ADA and create precedent.

sections.title: Risk review
missing: independent assurance
rollback/remedy path
dependency map
sections.conclusion: Risk is not a side note; unmitigated execution or governance risk can dominate an otherwise attractive proposal.

sections.title: Counterargument pass
findings: Strongest YES: the proposal substantiates "An Info governance action titled Cardanoの生きがい - Ikigai - was submitted in September 2024 soon after the Chang hard fork." and clears the evidence gates.

Strongest NO: a material claim is unsupported — "A Cardano node bug permitted an unregistered stake key to be used in the governance action, preventing the submitter from recovering the 100,000 ADA deposit." — so cost or precedent may outweigh the benefit.
Strongest hold: if claims cannot be tied to replayable evidence, abstaining avoids overclaiming certainty.
sections.conclusion: A defensible rationale must show the best opposing case before it reaches a vote.

sections.title: Synthesis
findings: Final vote must be derived from completed sections above, not from a prose summary.
The public rationale should name the decisive section and the strongest counterargument.
sections.conclusion: The vote is only credible if the assessment tree shows enough work for a skeptical delegator to audit.

flags.detail: No links to forum discussion or community feedback
Treasury withdrawal to a single address

treasury_capacity.caveat: Set by an Info governance action. Info actions change no ledger state and can NEVER be enacted -- they always expire -- so no formally ratified NCL exists or can exist. This is the strongest available public chain evidence: an anchor document byte-verified against its on-chain blake2b-256 hash, covering the current epoch, whose voting CLOSED with a majority of participating DRep stake. It is NOT enacted ledger state, and the majority may fall short of the supermajority other action types require. Published with every treasury rationale that relies on it.
